other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant

Section 33 of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 provides that an authorised officer of Revenue and Customs may arrest a person without warrant if the officer reasonably suspects that the person has committed an offence under this section, or is committing or is about to commit such an offence. Authorised means authorised by the Commissioners. Authorisation for the purposes of this section may be specific or general.
other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

In relation to offences committed before the commencement of section 282 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003: six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
